title: Low pay at the Spotlight cabaret and advice to young players
summary: He recalls working for a dollar and a half a night at the Spotlight with Jerry Cooper and others, and says players should stick to the melody.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Jerry Cooper, the singer. He's up, uh, he's up in New York. He left in and he never did come back. There was Jerry Cooper, myself, Candy Candina, uh, Coco, and, uh, Joe Valenti. He's playing bass now. And, uh, I don't know who was on the drums at that time. But that was in a spotlight. They had a night club in them days. Cabaret, they called them. That's what they called them in those days. Cabarets. And we were all playing in that same place for a dollar and a half a night. And if we'd have gotten a break that some of these musicians are fortunate enough to get today, I think we'd have all been on the top too. But it just came too late for a lot of us. That's the reason why we all washed up. And we were all playing in the middle of the night. Because it's too late in life to start over. That's what my view about the thing. And I say, if all these musicians that's coming up, these young ones, they just put their mind to, if, if they're gonna play Dixieland, they ought to try to stick to the lead mostly. Instead of trying to vary it all over the horn and the public don't know what they're playing. I often think if they'll stick to the lead, they'll wind up being better musicians. And playing all this kind of music that they want to play these days. I don't know. It just defeats me. I can't understand that maybe I'm in a different category. That's all. Times has changed, like I say. You know what I mean? Like the college students and all might go for progressive music these days. I don't know. And bebop and all. But that's not music to it. Somebody would've trained me. I said, I want to stick more around melody. I think they'd wind up better. My viewpoint of it is that I always liked to variate too. But I always did fall back on melody to find out where I was. Because sometimes you could be very varied on out in the clouds. So if you stare out at Leeds, you're gonna find out where you are. I think musicians these days, they always changing. I mean, I don't know. I guess they're just moving into another world.
